transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-11
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Avery Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sara Nguyen (Hearthline Head Procurement), Tom Ellis (Hearthline CISO), Priya Kaur (VP Eng), Markus Lehtinen (Finance), K. Adler (external counsel, dropped early)

Summary: quick tabletop to map contract pathways, data residency/egress concerns, SLAs, and who needs to sign off. Not a redline session, but clarifying acceptance tolerances and path-to-production gating items.

Topics: MSA vs DPA exceptions, SLA credit models, KMS/HSM needs, data residency and egress charges, pricing acceptance path, timeline to pilot, security docs link references.

00:00 Avery: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, i think we all have the agenda — quick tabletop to map out the contract and procurement path, um i'll run through high level and diego will cover the technical failure modes and private options.
00:18 Sara: thanks avery, appreciate it. we just need to be clear about data residency and egress costs — finance will flag any recurring egress fees.
00:30 Markus: yep, finance is sensitive to per-GB egress. also want clarity on SLA credits and when we can terminate without penalty.
00:45 Diego: (SE) yeah, i'll walk through routing and fallback; there are hosted and private deployment options, and the default hosted path has regional controls but not customer-managed KMS unless you pick private.
01:05 Tom: so on the KMS question, do you offer customer-managed keys in the VPC/private deployment? is HSM supported?
01:13 Avery: short answer — yes on private deployments we support external KMS/HSM integrations, we also provide bring-your-own-key workflows. on hosted we offer tenant encryption with our KMS, + options for dedicated key wrapping by agreement.
01:30 Priya: what about audit logs and access? we need per-request auditability for HIPAA workflows.
01:38 Diego: we emit audit logs, token-level traces — console retention varies by plan. for Private you can ship logs to your SIEM via our syslog/HTTP forwarders; hosted has an export option but retention is shorter unless you pick the premium observability add-on.
02:02 Sara: legal will want DPA terms that clearly say no human review for PHI — is that in the standard DPA?
02:12 Avery: our standard DPA restricts usage and describes handling; we can surface clause language. if you need explicit PHI no-human-review clause we can propose it as an addendum — we'll flag that to legal.
02:30 Markus: what about termination and data return/secure-delete? we need guarantees and a certificate of deletion.
02:40 Avery: we provide data egress and deletion commitments in MSA; we can include a certificate-of-destruction workflow for Private deployments; for hosted we'll outline the export + deletion SLA.
03:00 Tom: is there any escrow for model artifacts, or for the service? some vendors do code escrow; will Redwood consider limited escrow for critical bits?
03:12 Avery: we've had requests for algorithmic escrow, but typically customers ask for operational runbooks and access to a fallback model. we can discuss escrow with legal, it's not standard but we can explore contractually.
03:30 Diego: on the SLA side, failure modes are: control plane outage (rare), regional GPU capacity constraints (burst), and model quality regressions. we provide automatic fallback routing to compatible model variants to keep latency but maybe degrade across quality tiers. credits are usually tied to availability windows and mean time to recovery.
03:55 Priya: can you quantify the credit model? like how many minutes before a credit kicks in?
04:03 Avery: typical is availability < 99.9% triggers credit bands — i'll include the table in the MSA redline. for Dedicated customers there's a higher SLA and faster recovery commitments.
04:20 Sara: payment terms — we need standard net-60 for vendors over $100k. any flexibility?
04:28 Markus: finance note: if we sign multi-year reserved capacity (dedicated) we need a 30-day termination for material breach and a pricing floor for budgeting.
04:44 Avery: we usually do net-30 for self-serve, but enterprise deals are negotiable; we'll include options for net-45/60 in the commercial addendum.
05:00 (brief crosstalk)
05:14 K. Adler: (drops in) sorry, legal — quick Q: indemnity for data breaches, is Redwood's liability capped?
05:22 Avery: our standard MSA has liability caps tied to fees paid over prior 12 months, but we can pull the specific carve-outs for data exfiltration and propose a higher cap for regulated customers; i'll surface the legal precedent.
05:40 Tom: also need SOC2 + ISO attestation or equivalent; do you have those ready?
05:48 Avery: yes we are SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, will share artifacts — link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (secure link).
06:00 Diego: technical point — Private on-prem package contains an air-gapped installer and a support window for security patching; that changes SLAs and support metrics.
06:16 Priya: timeline: if we want a pilot with PHI redaction flow in our environment, how long to stand up private?
06:24 Diego: estimate 6-8 weeks for on-prem with our team + your infra; VPC-private (managed customer VPC) is 3-4 weeks typically. hosted pilot can start in days with restricted datasets and synthetic tests.
06:40 Sara: and from procurement's perspective, we need to know who's signing — legal, procurement, and security sign-off. we'll need price + DPA redline to route to legal.
06:54 Avery: understood, we'll send the redline bundle. i'll include a summary of differences to make review quicker.
07:08 Markus: one more — egress pricing. what's your model if we archive logs or call transcripts off-platform?
07:17 Avery: egress is charged per-GB for data extraction from hosted regions; for Dedicated there's an included threshold in reserved capacity, then overage. we'll put the detailed table in the commercial sheet.
07:34 Tom: about data residency — we need all production inference for EU patients to stay in eu-west-1, can you guarantee region pinning?
07:44 Diego: yes we support region pinning. in hosted mode we route to the pinned region; for compliance-critical workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private to eliminate cross-region routing.
08:02 Priya: can you provide a sample network diagram showing endpoint placement, NAT, VPC peering, and where KMS lives?
08:10 Diego: yes, i'll attach network diagram + sample terraform snippet for VPC peering.
08:18 Sara: allow me to ask — what's the escalation ladder if a security incident impacts us? do you have a runbook and notification SLA?
08:27 Avery: yes, we have incident response SLA: initial ack < 60 min for Sev1, primary contact 24x7, and status updates; we'll share the escalation ladder.
08:40 K. Adler: (again) when you share the DPA please highlight any subprocessor list and if you have the right to add subprocessors unilaterally. that's a sticking point for us.
08:52 Avery: we'll annotate subprocessors and propose a 30-day notice clause for additions or an approval-run where critical subprocessors require mutual consent.
09:05 Priya: in terms of model updates, is there a rollback policy if a new model weights rollout degrades outputs?
09:12 Diego: yes, we support canary rollouts and automatic rollback triggers keyed off quality monitors; we can also pin model versions per-customer to avoid surprises.
09:28 Markus: who owns the evals? like if we detect regression, do you reimburse?
09:34 Avery: we track quality SLAs separately and for enterprise we can negotiate remedies — usually operational mitigations first, credits in severe cases.
09:48 Sara: ok, sounds like next step is to get your redline and security docs. also please list the specific MSA clauses you expect negotiation on (liability, IP, subcontracting, termination, data retention).
10:02 Avery: will do, i'll include a 'clause tracker' so legal can go clause-by-clause.
10:10 Tom: small ask — can you provide a short tech-runbook showing the steps to failover to a secondary region? our sysops will need it.
10:18 Diego: yes will include a 1-pager runbook + escalation path.
10:24 (silence, brief keyboard sounds)
10:30 Avery: i'll recap after avery — next steps as we said. send the docs, schedule the exec steering call.
10:40 Sara: estimated internal timeline — procurement can route once legal has redline and finance has confirmed PO terms; probably 2 weeks from receipt.
10:52 Markus: tentative target: pilot in prod sandbox by early July if we clear the contract by mid-May.
11:05 Priya: we also want a short 1-hour technical deep dive for engs next week, can diego run that?
11:12 Diego: yes can do — i'll prepare targeted topics: VPC peering, KMS flows, KV cache behavior, and model pinning.
11:24 Avery: great. any final Qs?
11:30 Tom: none from me.
11:34 Sara: none, thanks all.
11:40 Avery: thanks everybody, i'll follow up with the bundle.

References shared in call: Security pack link (secure): https://redwood.example.com/security-pack; Draft MSA/DPA template location: internal redwood link (to be shared to customer via secure drive).

End of transcript.
notes: Tabletop framing avoided clause-level negotiation in-call; focus was on acceptance gates and timelines.
Customer sensitive to egress fees and KMS ownership; Private deployment is likely to be preferred for PHI workloads.
Redwood to prioritize redline + security pack; exec steering call will accelerate commercial approval.
